title: Aspect Deep 4: Aspect in the Imperative
description: Imperatives carry aspect. Pf imperative for one specific request (Прочитай!), impf for habitual or process commands (Читай!). Negative pf for warnings against accidents (Не разбей!).
descriptionRussian: В повелительном наклонении вид меняет смысл. СВ для конкретной просьбы (Прочитай!), НСВ для общей или повторяющейся команды (Читай!). Не + СВ для предупреждения о случайности (Не разбей!).
intro: The A2 imperative book covered this ground, and this lesson pushes on the part that stays slippery: the negative. A plain prohibition and a warning against an accident use opposite aspects, and the sentences look almost identical. The question to ask is whether you are stating a rule or heading off one specific mishap.
rules: Positive imperative: perfective for a single specific request (Прочитай! Купи! Сделай!), imperfective for habit, process, or general command (Читай! Пиши! Делай!).
Negative imperative default: не + imperfective for a standard prohibition (Не пей это! Не открывай дверь! Не делай этого!).
Negative imperative special: не + perfective as a warning against an accidental, undesired completion (Не разбей вазу! Не упади! Не забудь!).
Diagnostic for negative imperatives: is this a general 'don't do this,' or a warning against a specific accident? Prohibition → impf; warning → pf.
examples: Прочитай статью к завтра. (Read the article by tomorrow.) Single specific request → СВ.
Читай каждый день! (Read every day!) Habitual command → НСВ.
Не пей холодную воду! (Don't drink cold water!) General prohibition → не + НСВ.
Не разбей вазу! (Don't [accidentally] break the vase!) Warning against accident → не + СВ.
Не забывай маму. (Don't forget Mom [as a habit].) General prohibition → не + НСВ.
Не забудь купить молоко! (Don't forget to buy milk!) Warning against a specific lapse → не + СВ.

items.promptEnglish: Masha finally finished this long book.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 3: which family is наконец-то in?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 3: наконец-то is an emphatic completion adverb and triggers the perfective. Past fem -ла: прочитала. Today's lesson moves the same impf-vs-pf choice into the imperative mood, where the choice carries a different kind of meaning.

items.promptEnglish: Read this article by tomorrow morning.
items.hint: Single specific request with a deadline. Which imperative form?
items.explanation: A single specific request with a deadline takes the perfective imperative: Прочитай. The imperfective Читай would be a habitual or general 'be reading' command, which the deadline rules out.

items.prompt: _____ эти статьи каждый день, и твой русский улучшится.
items.promptEnglish: Read these articles every day, and your Russian will improve.
items.hint: Каждый день is a frequency cue. Habit → which imperative?
items.explanation: Каждый день frames the command as a habit, not a one-shot request. The imperfective imperative Читай carries the habitual reading. Прочитай would describe a single completed act, which 'every day' contradicts.

items.promptEnglish: Don't drink cold water, you'll get sick.
items.hint: Standard prohibition. Default negative imperative aspect?
items.explanation: A standard 'don't do this' prohibition uses не + imperfective imperative: не пей. The perfective не выпей would be a warning against accidentally drinking it all in one go, which the long-term illness reasoning does not target.

items.promptEnglish: Don't [accidentally] break the vase, it's very expensive!
items.hint: Warning against a specific accident. Which negative imperative aspect?
items.explanation: The speaker is not forbidding the listener from breaking vases in general; they are warning against the specific accident with this expensive vase. Warning → не + perfective imperative: не разбей. The imperfective не разбивай would suggest the listener has been habitually breaking vases.

items.prompt: _____ домашнее задание сейчас, у тебя экзамен завтра.
items.promptEnglish: Do your homework now, you have an exam tomorrow.
items.hint: Single specific request, with a deadline. Imperative aspect?
items.explanation: One specific homework session, with a deadline (завтра). Perfective imperative: Сделай. The imperfective Делай would be a general 'be doing your homework' (habit / process) command, which the urgency rules out.

items.promptEnglish: Get the homework done - the teacher will check it tomorrow.
items.hint: One specific job to complete: which imperative?
items.explanation: A single bounded request takes the perfective imperative: Сделай уроки. Делай is the habitual imperfective command.

items.promptEnglish: Read articles regularly - it's good for you.
items.explanation: A regular habit takes the imperfective imperative: Читай статьи регулярно. Прочитай would order one specific read-through.

items.promptEnglish: Don't forget about the meeting - it's very important.
items.hint: A one-time warning about one specific meeting.
items.explanation: A warning against one specific lapse takes не + perfective: Не забудь о встрече. Не забывай is a general habit-prohibition ('don't be forgetful'), broader than this one meeting.

items.prompt: _____ хлеб в магазине по дороге домой.
items.promptEnglish: Buy bread at the shop on your way home (one specific errand).
items.explanation: One specific errand takes the perfective imperative: Купи хлеб. Покупай would prescribe habitual buying.

items.promptEnglish: Write to your grandmother more often - she misses you.
items.explanation: The habit command takes the imperfective: Пиши чаще. Напиши would order one specific letter; the 'чаще' cue marks an ongoing pattern.

items.promptEnglish: Don't open that door - there's a storeroom behind it.
items.hint: A standing prohibition: which aspect under не?
items.explanation: A standing rule takes не + imperfective: Не открывай эту дверь. Не открой would warn about one specific accidental act, not state a permanent rule.

items.prompt: _____ на встречу: начальник этого не любит.
items.promptEnglish: Don't be late for the meeting (a warning against one specific lapse).
items.hint: A warning against one accidental result.
items.explanation: A warning against one specific accidental completion takes не + perfective: Не опоздай. Не опаздывай is the habit-prohibition ('stop being chronically late').

blanks: Не _____ купить молоко по дороге домой! (Don't forget to buy milk on the way home!)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: A specific reminder against a single lapse (forgetting this one errand) is a warning against an accidental result. Не + perfective imperative: не забудь. The imperfective не забывай would frame forgetting as a habit, which a one-time errand does not call for.

errorCorrection.sentence: Готовь ужин к семи часам: вечером придут гости.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Have dinner ready by seven; guests are coming tonight.
errorCorrection.explanation: A single specific request with a deadline ('к семи часам') takes the perfective imperative: Приготовь. The imperfective Готовь is the habit or process command ('do the cooking', 'be cooking'), which the one-time deadline contradicts. Positive imperative rule: perfective for one bounded request, imperfective for a general or repeated one.

errorCorrection.sentence: Никогда не опоздай на уроки, учитель этого не любит.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Never be late to your lessons; the teacher doesn't like it.
errorCorrection.explanation: A standing, habitual prohibition uses не + imperfective imperative: не опаздывай. The cue 'никогда' (never, ever) makes the command general and recurring, which only the imperfective carries. The perfective опоздай is the special 'don't [accidentally] be late this once' warning, which clashes with 'never, ever'. Default negative imperative: не + imperfective for a general prohibition.

errorCorrection.sentence: Осторожно, не падай на лестнице, там скользко!
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Careful, don't fall on the stairs, it's slippery!
errorCorrection.explanation: This is a warning against a specific, accidental result ('осторожно', 'там скользко'), which takes не + perfective imperative: не упади. The imperfective не падай is a general 'don't (keep) falling' prohibition, which does not fit a one-time caution about slippery stairs. Negative imperative split: a general prohibition uses не + imperfective; a warning against an accident uses не + perfective.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Take this medicine now (one specific dose).
minimalPairs.explanation: One specific dose right now is a single completed act. Perfective imperative: Выпей. The imperfective Пей would frame it as a habit or process, which 'now, this dose' does not match.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Drink water every day; it's good for you.
minimalPairs.explanation: Каждый день frames the command as a habit. Imperfective imperative: Пей. The perfective Выпей would describe a single completed drinking act, which 'every day' rules out.

reviewVocab.definition: the imperative mood (commands and requests; aspect choice in the imperative changes whether the command is single or habitual, prohibition or warning)
reviewVocab.example: В повелительном наклонении вид часто меняет смысл просьбы.

reviewVocab.definition: prohibition (the standard 'don't do this' negative imperative; takes не + imperfective: 'Не пей это!')
reviewVocab.example: Запрет обычно выражается через не + НСВ: 'Не открывай эту дверь.'

reviewVocab.definition: warning (here: 'don't accidentally do this'; takes не + perfective imperative: 'Не разбей вазу!')
reviewVocab.example: Предупреждение об опасности часто звучит как не + СВ: 'Не упади!'
